why: I checked all five expect lines and their proofs. Each one can be checked at the PR head before merge with one clear answer. Lines 1, 2 and 5 are `node -e` commands with exact exit-code checks (e.g. `Object.is(r,0)`). Line 3 is "`npm test` exits 0 on the pull request head". Line 4 reads test/math.test.js and runs `git show main:math.js > math.js && node --test; echo $?`. This needs only the local main branch, which exists before merge, and it says how to restore the file with `git checkout -- math.js`. Every proof is `run` with exact commands and the expected status. No line needs a release, deploy, published page or anything that exists only after merge. Publishing a version is explicitly listed as a non-goal.
